_note: K-Food tab searches (both editions), one group per theme; each group runs first_run searches on its first night, then per_night in rotation (100 YouTube API units each).

groups.name: konbini
groups._note: K-Food tab (both editions): popular shorts of Korean convenience-store tours and finds — drink combos, cup-ramyeon machines, new snacks — and Han River ramyeon / picnics, from Korean and foreign creators. YouTube searches (100 API units each): first_run on the first night, then per_night in rotation. Added 2026-10-27 (per David).

groups.name: pilgrimage
groups._note: K-Food tab (both editions): fans visiting the places of popular idols — filming locations, the restaurants and cafes they went to (K-pop pilgrimage / 성지순례). Added 2026-10-27 (per David).

groups.name: heritage
groups._note: Traditional Seoul (both editions): palaces, Bukchon / Seochon / Buam-dong / Ikseon-dong / Insadong, Jongno pojangmacha, hanbok rental with hair styling and hanbok shopping, and nearby cafes and restaurants. Hanbok-wearing palace visitors rose from 0.54M (2022) to 2.0M (2024), +268% (Korea Heritage Service, Hankyung 2025-11-23). Added 2026-10-27 (per David).

groups.name: busan
groups._note: Busan (both editions): the spots, markets, restaurants, cafes and tours foreign visitors favour — Haeundae (Blueline Park sky capsule), Gwangalli drone show, Gamcheon and Huinnyeoul villages, Jagalchi / Gukje / Kkangtong markets, Nampo-BIFF street food, Haedong Yonggungsa, Jeonpo cafe street, Yeongdo cafes, Millac The Market. Busan had 2.42M foreign visitors in H1 2026 (+43.9%); nearly 60% planned to shop at traditional markets (Korea Times 2026-08-01, Stars and Stripes). Added 2026-10-27 (per David).
